title: How to Hire Help to Manage an Amazon Store
h1: How to hire help to manage an Amazon store
description: Hire help for an Amazon store: tasks to hand over, access and safety, listing and ads work, reporting, coaching versus management and what to ask first.
intro: Running an Amazon store involves many recurring jobs: product listings, inventory, customer messages, advertising, reviews and reports. Some sellers hire a virtual assistant, a consultant or an account manager to share the load. Giving someone access to a store is a trust decision, so preparation matters. This article explains how to plan the help, protect your account and judge the work.

faq.q: Should I hire a coach, an assistant or a manager?
faq.a: A coach teaches you to run the store, an assistant handles routine tasks, and a manager takes responsibility for results. Pick the role that matches how involved you want to be.

faq.q: Is it safe to give access to my seller account?
faq.a: Use the platform's own user permissions, give only the access needed and never share your main password.

faq.q: What tasks can be handed over?
faq.a: Listing updates, inventory checks, customer message replies, advertising reports, product research and routine reporting are common.

faq.q: How do I measure the work?
faq.a: Agree on a few numbers such as sales, advertising cost, response time and listing quality, and review them regularly.
Set a budget and rules. Ask for regular reports on spend and results.
